name: AQ-400 Scythe
representative_system: AQ-400 Scythe — One-way attack drone (deep strike, volunteer-developed)

cost.display: Not publicly disclosed; deliberately low-cost design philosophy

characteristics: Strength: Deliberately optimized for cheap, fast production (Terminal Autonomy volunteer project) rather than aerodynamic refinement - trades some performance for producibility and cost
Limitation: Shorter range than some competitors (Beaver, Zozulia) though with a heavier payload option
Estimated quantity available: In serial production; exact numbers not disclosed
employment_notes: A volunteer-originated project that reached serial production - a direct example of the decentralized, bottom-up defense-industry pattern (mirrored by Lithuania's VytisTech/Ukraine's Brave1 model) rather than top-down state design
contrast_vs_traditional: Volunteer-developed rather than centrally programmed, Scythe is another instance of the doctrine.md force-structure finding that procurement for this class of system is often decentralized — a deep-strike capability fielded because a unit or developer built one, not because a traditional acquisition process specified and funded it.

sources.label: Militarnyi — Ukrainian military received AQ-400 Scythe UAVs
